outcome: Since 26 January 2024 the general Farrell–Jones conjecture remains unresolved, with no counterexample reported; the in-window results are class-level or single-group cases (Durham–Minsky–Sisto for colorable hierarchically hyperbolic groups, first posted 23 April 2025; Roushon's February 2024 corrigendum and Li–Roushon's March 2024 preprint on affine Artin groups of type B~n), and no AI system was found to be involved in any of them.
problem_asks: (1) K-theoretic part: for every discrete group G, with no restriction on G, and for the coefficient rings the conjecture is stated for, the assembly map H^G_n(E_VCYC(G); K_R) -> K_n(R[G]) is an isomorphism for all integers n. (2) L-theoretic part: the same question for the assembly map H^G_n(E_VCYC(G); L_R) -> L_n(R[G]) into the L-theory of group rings, for all n. (3) The bullet says 'certain assembly maps' and does not name the family of subgroups. The classical version (Farrell–Jones 1993, and the Wikipedia article's formulation) uses the family of virtually cyclic subgroups; the 'full' version (Lück) uses a larger family. The bullet is read as asking whether the conjecture holds for all groups, in whichever family it is stated. (4) The bullet is a yes-or-no question about all groups. A positive result for a class of groups, a class of coefficient rings, or a class of invariants answers a restricted version only.

events.what_happened: Matthew Gentry Durham, Yair Minsky and Alessandro Sisto, 'Asymptotically CAT(0) metrics, Z-structures, and the Farrell–Jones Conjecture' (arXiv:2504.17048; v1 23 April 2025 only, as of 11 October 2026; 84 pp; no journal reference on arXiv). Proves that colorable hierarchically hyperbolic groups (HHGs) admit asymptotically CAT(0) metrics, uses them to build contractible complexes and Z-structures in the sense of Bestvina–Dranishnikov, and deduces the Farrell–Jones conjecture (FJC) for many HHGs. Per the HTML text: Theorem C reduces FJC for a colorable HHG (G, S) to FJC for the stabilizers Stab(U) of the pieces U not ⊑-maximal; Corollary D states 'Decomposable HHGs satisfy the Farrell–Jones Conjecture'; Corollary E covers extra-large-type Artin groups; the paper says Corollary D recovers the FJC for mapping class groups already proven by Bartels–Bestvina. Sisto gave talks on the work from 2023 and at Münster on 23 Feb 2026; the first public written argument is the arXiv v1, so this is the dating event.
events.delivers: FJC for colorable HHGs, conditional on FJC for the stabilizers in Theorem C; and, per Corollary D as quoted, FJC for decomposable HHGs (hyperbolic groups are decomposable by definition, and the paper's examples include extra-large-type Artin groups and quotients of mapping class groups by large powers of Dehn twists). I did not check whether Corollary D depends on Theorem C's hypothesis, or how 'decomposable' relates to 'colorable'. It also establishes that colorable HHGs, including mapping class groups, are asymptotically CAT(0) and admit Z-structures.
events.remains: The conjecture for all groups; for all HHGs (the Sisto survey asks this as Question 5.4); for non-colorable HHGs, which are outside Theorem C's hypothesis (the Sisto survey says Hagen's non-colourable examples are cubical and so covered by Bartels–Lück [BL12]; I did not verify that).
events.direction: Confirms the conjecture for the classes stated (colorable HHGs under Theorem C; decomposable HHGs per Corollary D). No counterexample. Cuts toward the conjecture; does not address the all-groups question.

events.what_happened: Wolfgang Lück, 'Survey on the Farrell–Jones Conjecture' (arXiv:2507.11337; submitted 15 July 2025; 36 pp; 'to appear in the Bulletin of the AMS'; no arXiv journal reference). An expository survey of the conjecture, its applications and its status. Section 11, 'Can the Full Farrell-Jones Conjecture be true for all groups?', lists classes where the full conjecture is open 'at the time of writing': elementary amenable, amenable and a-T-menable groups; Out(F_n) for n ≥ 3; Artin groups; Thompson's groups F, V, T; torsion-free one-relator groups; linear groups; subgroups of almost connected Lie groups; residually finite groups; (bi-)automatic groups; locally indicable groups. States that the class known to satisfy the full conjecture contains hyperbolic groups, finite-dimensional CAT(0) groups, lattices, fundamental groups of manifolds of dimension at most 3, and S-arithmetic groups, and that no group is known for which the full conjecture is false. In the text read, it does not cite Durham–Minsky–Sisto or Andrew–Guerch–Hughes.
events.delivers: No new theorem. A status survey: the full conjecture is known for a large class, open in general, and no counterexample is known.
events.remains: The full conjecture for all groups.
events.direction: No result, so no direction. Its status statements agree that the all-groups question is open.

disputes.summary: Roushon's affine Artin group claim for B~n (n ≥ 3). The 2018/2020 paper claimed the Farrell–Jones isomorphism conjecture for these groups, relying on Proposition 4.1, which J. Flechsig identified as erroneous. The February 2024 corrigendum replaces it with the wreath-product form FICwF (as its reported theorem states), but its abstract, as fetched, still speaks of 'the Farrell-Jones isomorphism conjecture' for these groups. The March 2024 Li–Roushon paper (Remark 1.1) states that the Farrell–Jones isomorphism conjecture holds for B~n, citing BFW. The sources do not reconcile these statements, and I did not read the corrigendum's full text.

summary: Since 26 January 2024 the general Farrell–Jones conjecture (FJC) appears unresolved. No source I opened, and no search result, reports a proof for all groups or a counterexample, and the Lück survey (July 2025) and the Sisto survey (July 2025) both record it as open; the Lück survey lists the classes where the full conjecture is still open, and Sisto's Question 5.4 asks the all-HHG case. Within the window the substantive results are class-level or single-group. (a) Durham–Minsky–Sisto, arXiv:2504.17048, first posted 23 April 2025 (v1 only), proves FJC for colorable hierarchically hyperbolic groups conditionally on FJC for stabilizers (Theorem C), and states FJC for decomposable HHGs (Corollary D); extra-large-type Artin groups are among the examples. I read about 94% of its HTML text; the acknowledgements are NSF grants and no AI statement appears. The Sisto survey (arXiv:2507.17546, July 2025; Sisto is a coauthor of DMS) cites it as proving FJC for 'most' HHGs; that is a citation by a coauthor, not an independent check, and I found no independent expert engagement with DMS. (b) Roushon's corrigendum to his 2018/2020 Artin-group paper (Canad. J. Math., online 23 February 2024) records an error in Proposition 4.1 for affine Artin groups of type B~n (n ≥ 3), identified by J. Flechsig, and replaces the claim with a wreath-product (FICwF) statement; its abstract still uses the full wording, so which result it delivers is close and I could not settle it without the full text. (c) Li and Roushon, arXiv:2403.09533 (14 March 2024; v2 24 October 2025; Bull. Sci. Math. 2026), show the affine Artin group of type B~n is virtually poly-free, and Remark 1.1 says that with BFW's theorem the Farrell–Jones isomorphism conjecture holds for that group; I did not verify the deduction, and the paper's abstract does not mention FJ. Close calls: whether a class-level theorem such as DMS counts as a case of the all-groups question (the question asks about all groups, so DMS settles a restricted version only); whether the Li–Roushon remark counts as a single-group case; and whether the corrigendum delivers FICwF or the full conjecture for B~n. Dating: the Andrew–Guerch–Hughes paper (arXiv:2311.14036) is dated to its v1 of 23 November 2023 and the Bunke–Kasprowski–Winges preprint (arXiv:2111.02490) to 3 November 2021, both before the window; their 2026 journal publications are not dating events under §5.1. The earlier run's record for this key (data/mark_2026-09-22/deepdive/out/farrell-jones-conjecture.json) used arXiv:2504.17048 as its load-bearing event and I confirm that; but it cites arXiv:2211.15523 as the Bunke–Kasprowski–Winges result, and that identifier is Reis's note, which I record separately (reis-2022-11). The earlier run also presented the Lück survey as digesting DMS; the portions of the survey I could read do not mention DMS. Other items I found and discounted as different questions: Bartels–Lück papers on Hecke algebras of totally disconnected groups (June 2023 postings), the Lück–Oliver Whitehead-group paper (June 2025), and Hamenstädt's EZ-structure for the mapping class group (May 2025), whose mapping class group case was already settled. On AI: I searched the problem name with Claude, GPT-5 and GPT-5.5 Pro, Gemini Deep Think, AlphaEvolve and AlphaProof, Lean, FrontierMath and Erdős-problem terms, and OpenAI's August 2026 'Astra' results. No source I opened or found credits an AI system with any Farrell–Jones result. The Astra list, as reported by secondary coverage, contains no Farrell–Jones item; the primary OpenAI document was unreadable, so this rests on secondary reports. The AlphaEvolve paper (November 2025) is described in a search snippet as covering analysis, combinatorics, geometry and number theory; I did not open it. Each event's ai.sources states how much of its text I read.
competing_reading: Read as a partial resolution, the window contains a real advance: DMS establishes FJC for a large class of groups (colorable HHGs, decomposable HHGs, including all hyperbolic groups, mapping class groups and extra-large Artin groups), and AGH's fibred results extend the known list, so the problem is 'known for more groups' than in January 2024. Read as a no-change result, nothing in the window touches the all-groups statement: DMS and AGH are restrictions; Roushon's corrected result and the Li–Roushon remark are single families of groups; the surveys record the conjecture as open; and the Roushon corrigendum's reported theorem is the weaker FICwF form, which the scope rule excludes. A reader who takes the Li–Roushon remark or the corrigendum's abstract at face value would count a single-group full case inside the window; a reader who takes the reported theorem would not. A reader who dates AGH by its 2026 Math. Ann. acceptance would move that paper into the window; the dating rule says not to.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full text of the Roushon corrigendum (or arXiv:1811.11589 v-final) to see whether the B~n theorem is FICwF or the full FJC. (2) The full text of Li–Roushon (arXiv:2403.09533 v2): the deduction from virtual poly-freeness to FJC for B~n, and whether it uses a finite-index subgroup or overgroup step, and if so whether that step is settled. (3) The remaining 6% of the DMS HTML text and any published version; and whether a later paper or expert review engages with DMS Theorem C and Corollary D. (4) Any independent review of DMS, or a 2026 citing paper that uses it as a published proof. (5) The Springer full text of arXiv:2311.14036 for its acknowledgements (AI check) and whether v2 adds results beyond v1. (6) The preface and table of contents of Lück's 2025 book, to see whether it contains new results. (7) OpenAI's primary 'Ten Advances' document, to confirm that no item concerns Farrell–Jones.

event.what_happened: S. K. Roushon, 'Corrigendum: A certain structure of Artin groups and the isomorphism conjecture', Canad. J. Math. 76(2) (2024), 729–730, DOI 10.4153/S0008414X24000191, published online 23 February 2024. Per the corrigendum page: 'Flechsig pointed out an error in' Proposition 4.1 of the original, 'which was needed to deduce the Farrell–Jones isomorphism conjecture' for affine Artin groups of type B~n (n ≥ 3). The corrigendum gives an alternate argument: it proves the Farrell–Jones isomorphism conjecture 'wreath product with finite groups' (FICwF) for these groups (n ≥ 3), using a hyperplane-arrangement complement, a homeomorphism of Callegaro–Moroni–Salvetti, results of Huang and Osajda, and finite-index orbifold covers. The corrigendum's abstract, as fetched, reads 'we give an alternate proof of the Farrell-Jones isomorphism conjecture for the affine Artin groups of type' (cut off in the fetched text). The corrigendum's full text was not read.
event.delivers: FICwF (Farrell–Jones with wreath products with finite groups) for affine Artin groups of type B~n, n ≥ 3, as the theorem is reported. A weaker form than the full conjecture. The corrigendum's abstract wording refers to 'the Farrell-Jones isomorphism conjecture' for these groups, which I could not reconcile with the reported FICwF theorem without the full text.
event.remains: The full Farrell–Jones conjecture for affine Artin groups of type B~n (n ≥ 3), unless the corrigendum's abstract is read as the full statement; the corrigendum's own reported theorem is the weaker FICwF.

judgement.why: The statement asks whether the assembly maps are isomorphisms for all groups, so every class-level theorem (hyperbolic, CAT(0), mapping class groups, colorable/decomposable HHGs, affine Artin B~n) is a case, never whole. DMS is an unreviewed but credible case by established authors; the Sisto survey is a coauthor's restatement, not digestion. The B~n corrigendum and Li–Roushon remark are journal-published cases kept as doubtful given the conceded earlier error and the unreconciled wording; whichever form (FICwF or plain FJC) the corrigendum delivers, it is a case for one family. The original 2018 claim is knocked down by the identified, conceded error in Proposition 4.1. Localising-invariant results: BKW still covers K-theory for its group classes, so case; Reis only removes an invariant-side hypothesis, so variant. Totally disconnected/Hecke-algebra work is an analogue (variant). Surveys, the book, the EZ-structure and the Whitehead-group paper settle nothing (none). No AI system is credited anywhere.
judgement.doubts: The record calls FICwF 'weaker' than the full conjecture; the wreath-product form is normally the stronger, inheritance-friendly version, which if anything strengthens the corrigendum's case, but its scope remains one family either way. Pre-snapshot journal verifications rest on search snippets. Recent (Sept–Oct 2026) postings may be missing.
